{{short description|American physicist (1936–1984)}}
'''William L. McMillan''' (January 13, 1936 – August 30, 1984) was an American [[physicist]] noted for his research of [[condensed matter physics]].
<ref name="ILLINOIS">{{Cite web |url=http://physics.illinois.edu/people/memorials/mcmillan.asp |title=Physics Illinois:Memorials:William L. McMillan |access-date=2012-01-07 |archive-date=2016-06-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160619001149/http://physics.illinois.edu/people/memorials/mcmillan.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref>
<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=10470&page=199 National Academies Press:Biographical Memoirs:V.81:WILLIAM L. MCMILLAN, BY P. W. ANDERSON]</ref>
<ref name="ACAP">{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?mcmillanw |title=Array of contemporary Physicists:William L. McMillan |access-date=2012-01-07 |archive-date=2016-03-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307155617/https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?mcmillanw |url-status=dead }}</ref>
McMillan was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], professor of physics at [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="NAP"/><ref name="ACAP"/>
He was also a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name="ACAP"/>
McMillan received the 1978 [[Fritz London Memorial Prize]] for his work in superconductors.<ref name="ACAP"/>
The [[National Academies Press]] called him "the ablest [[condensed matter]] physicist of his generation".<ref name="NAP"/>
The [[University of Illinois]] established an award in his name: The William L. McMillan Award.<ref>[http://physics.illinois.edu/about/mcmillan/winners.asp University of Illinois:Winners of the McMillan Award]</ref>

The electron-phonon coupling in superconductors is described by the McMillan parameter.

== Life and career ==
* 1936 born in Little Rock, Arkansas<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1958: BS, [[University of Arkansas]] (Electrical Engineering)<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1959: MS, [[University of Arkansas]] (Physics)<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1964: PhD, [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]]<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1964–1972: [[Bell Laboratories]], Member, Technical Staff<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1972–1984: [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]], Professor of Physics<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1978 [[Fritz London Memorial Prize]] for his work on superconductors
* 1982: elected to [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="ACAP"/>
* 1983: elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1983<ref name="ILLINOIS"/>
* 1984: Died of an accident at age 48
